solution:
The region is the rectangle \(0 \le x \le 5,\ 0 \le y \le 2\).
Taking the area under \(y=2\) from \(x=0\) to \(x=5\):
\(A = \int_0^5 y\,dx = \int_0^5 2\,dx = [\,2x\,]_0^5 = 10 - 0 = 10\).
\(A = 10\) sq. units.

Region under \(y=\sin x\), the X-axis, from \(x=0\) to \(x=\pi\).
\(A = \int_0^{\pi} y\,dx = \int_0^{\pi} \sin x\,dx = [\,-\cos x\,]_0^{\pi} = -\cos\pi + \cos 0 = -(-1) + 1 = 2\).
\(A = 2\) sq. units.

Region under \(y=\sin x\), the X-axis, from \(x=0\) to \(x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(A = \int_0^{\pi/3} \sin x\,dx = [\,-\cos x\,]_0^{\pi/3} = -\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \cos 0 = -\dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(A = \dfrac{1}{2}\) sq. units.

The circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) has radius \(3\) and is symmetric about both axes, so its area is \(4\) times the first-quadrant area where \(y=\sqrt{9-x^2}\).
\(A = 4\int_0^3 y\,dx = 4\int_0^3 \sqrt{9-x^2}\,dx\).
Using \(\int \sqrt{a^2-x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2-x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\) with \(a=3\):
\(A = 4\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{9-x^2} + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{3}\right]_0^3 = 4\left[\,0 + \dfrac{9}{2}\sin^{-1}(1)\,\right] = 4\cdot\dfrac{9}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 9\pi\).
\(A = 9\pi\) sq. units.

For the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1\), \(a=5,\ b=4\). In the first quadrant \(y = \dfrac{4}{5}\sqrt{25-x^2}\). By symmetry about both axes the area is \(4\) times the first-quadrant area.
\(A = 4\int_0^5 \dfrac{4}{5}\sqrt{25-x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{16}{5}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{25-x^2} + \dfrac{25}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{5}\right]_0^5\).
\(= \dfrac{16}{5}\left[\,0 + \dfrac{25}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\right] = \dfrac{16}{5}\cdot\dfrac{25\pi}{4} = 20\pi\).
\(A = 20\pi\) sq. units.

Curves: \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2=4y\). For intersection put \(y=\dfrac{x^2}{4}\) in \(y^2=4x\): \(\dfrac{x^4}{16}=4x \Rightarrow x^4=64x \Rightarrow x(x^3-64)=0 \Rightarrow x=0,\ 4\). Points \((0,0)\) and \((4,4)\).
Between them the upper curve is \(y=2\sqrt{x}\) (from \(y^2=4x\)) and the lower is \(y=\dfrac{x^2}{4}\).
\(A = \int_0^4\left(2\sqrt{x}-\dfrac{x^2}{4}\right)dx = \left[\dfrac{4}{3}x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^3}{12}\right]_0^4 = \dfrac{4}{3}(8) - \dfrac{64}{12} = \dfrac{32}{3} - \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{16}{3}\).
\(A = \dfrac{16}{3}\) sq. units.

Curves: \(4y^2=9x\) and \(3x^2=16y\). From the first \(x=\dfrac{4y^2}{9}\); put in the second: \(3\left(\dfrac{4y^2}{9}\right)^2=16y \Rightarrow \dfrac{48y^4}{81}=16y \Rightarrow y^4=27y \Rightarrow y(y^3-27)=0 \Rightarrow y=0,\ 3\). Then \(x=0,\ 4\); points \((0,0)\) and \((4,3)\).
Between them the upper curve is \(y=\dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}\) (from \(4y^2=9x\)) and the lower is \(y=\dfrac{3x^2}{16}\) (from \(3x^2=16y\)).
\(A = \int_0^4\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}-\dfrac{3x^2}{16}\right)dx = \left[x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^3}{16}\right]_0^4 = 8 - \dfrac{64}{16} = 8 - 4 = 4\).
\(A = 4\) sq. units.

Curves: \(y^2=x\) and \(x^2=y\). For intersection put \(y=x^2\) in \(y^2=x\): \(x^4=x \Rightarrow x(x^3-1)=0 \Rightarrow x=0,\ 1\). Points \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\).
Between them the upper curve is \(y=\sqrt{x}\) (from \(y^2=x\)) and the lower is \(y=x^2\).
\(A = \int_0^1(\sqrt{x}-x^2)\,dx = \left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}\).
\(A = \dfrac{1}{3}\) sq. units.

Region in the first quadrant bounded by the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) (radius \(2\)), the X-axis and the line \(x=\sqrt{3}\,y\).
The line meets the circle where \(3y^2+y^2=4 \Rightarrow y=1,\ x=\sqrt{3}\), i.e. at \((\sqrt{3},1)\); the line makes \(30^\circ\) with the X-axis.
Split the region at \(x=\sqrt{3}\): under the line \(y=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\) for \(0\le x\le\sqrt{3}\), and under the circle \(y=\sqrt{4-x^2}\) for \(\sqrt{3}\le x\le 2\).
\(A = \int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\,dx + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx\).
\(\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
\(\int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4-x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} = \left(0+2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \pi - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
\(A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(A = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\) sq. units.

Parabola \(y^2=x\) and line \(y=x\) meet where \(y^2=y \Rightarrow y=0,\ 1\); points \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\). In the first quadrant the parabola \(y=\sqrt{x}\) lies above the line \(y=x\).
\(A = \int_0^1(\sqrt{x}-x)\,dx = \left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = \dfrac{2}{3}-\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{6}\).
\(A = \dfrac{1}{6}\) sq. units.

Circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) and line \(x+y=1\) meet in the first quadrant at \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\). Between them the circle \(y=\sqrt{1-x^2}\) is above the line \(y=1-x\).
\(A = \int_0^1\left[\sqrt{1-x^2}-(1-x)\right]dx\).
\(\int_0^1\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-x^2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x\right]_0^1 = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).
\(\int_0^1(1-x)\,dx = \left[x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = 1-\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(A = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(A = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\) sq. units.

Parabola \((y-1)^2=4(x+1)\) (vertex \((-1,1)\), opening to the right) and line \(y=x-1\), i.e. \(x=y+1\).
Intersections: \((y-1)^2=4(y+1+1)=4y+8 \Rightarrow y^2-2y+1=4y+8 \Rightarrow y^2-6y-7=0 \Rightarrow (y-7)(y+1)=0 \Rightarrow y=-1,\ 7\), giving points \((0,-1)\) and \((8,7)\).
Integrate with respect to \(y\); the line \(x=y+1\) lies to the right of the parabola \(x=\dfrac{(y-1)^2}{4}-1\).
\(A = \int_{-1}^{7}\left[(y+1)-\left(\dfrac{(y-1)^2}{4}-1\right)\right]dy = \int_{-1}^{7}\left[y+2-\dfrac{(y-1)^2}{4}\right]dy = \dfrac{1}{4}\int_{-1}^{7}(-y^2+6y+7)\,dy\).
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[-\dfrac{y^3}{3}+3y^2+7y\right]_{-1}^{7} = \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{245}{3}-\left(-\dfrac{11}{3}\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{256}{3} = \dfrac{64}{3}\).
\(A = \dfrac{64}{3}\) sq. units.

Line \(2y=5x+7 \Rightarrow y=\dfrac{5x+7}{2}\), bounded by the X-axis and the lines \(x=2,\ x=5\).
\(A = \int_2^5 y\,dx = \int_2^5 \dfrac{5x+7}{2}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{5x^2}{2}+7x\right]_2^5\).
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\left(\dfrac{125}{2}+35\right)-\left(10+14\right)\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{195}{2}-24\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{147}{2} = \dfrac{147}{4}\).
\(A = \dfrac{147}{4}\) sq. units.

Curve \(y=4x^2 \Rightarrow x^2=\dfrac{y}{4} \Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\sqrt{y}}{2}\) (first quadrant), bounded by the Y-axis and the lines \(y=1,\ y=4\). Integrate with respect to \(y\):
\(A = \int_1^4 x\,dy = \int_1^4 \dfrac{\sqrt{y}}{2}\,dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{3}y^{3/2}\right]_1^4 = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[y^{3/2}\right]_1^4 = \dfrac{1}{3}(8-1) = \dfrac{7}{3}\).
\(A = \dfrac{7}{3}\) sq. units.
